title: Fix wslog parameters altering command line arguments
description:
Convert wslog subsystem to use ws_getopt subsystem to parse the command line arguments it's interested in rather than a independent solution that can modify the argc/argv parameters provided to an application. This way the argc/argv parameters aren't ever modified and cli_main.c can "own" their memory (and allocate and free as needed).
This means that all applications that use ws_log subsystem must provide the ws_log command line arguments in their list of "long" (command line) options.

Fix #20500

notes.body:
This "works" but wanted feedback on if it's the right approach in terms of encapsulation/layering.  wslog was a little more "self-contained" before this change, but I don't think it should be altering argc/argv parameters (which led to the bug).
wslog needs to share the "application" options because ws_getopt needs to know the "properties" of an option (and if they have a required argument) in order to properly parse any/all of them (as I found out testing with pytest)

Also, not sure if this should be backported for #20500.  For that, I think I like Guy's suggestion of copying the argc/argv memory more because it's less intrusive.

Unfortunately, a lot of the programs depended on `ws_log_parse_args` altering the command line arguments, and then later call `ws_getopt_log` and don't handle the logging options (expecting them to be gone).

So most programs, e.g., tshark, end up printing their usage and exiting if a logging option is given  (this is breaking the fuzz tests, which pass `--log-fatal-domains=UTF-8`), though `dftest` just asserts and fails:

```
$ ./run/dftest --log-level=debug 'tcp.port == 80'
 ** (dftest:810434) 06:37:58.888057 [Main ERROR] dftest.c:460 -- main(): assertion "not reached" failed
 ** (dftest:810434) Aborting on fatal log level exception
Aborted (core dumped)
```
Probably more programs need to use `ws_log_is_wslog_arg(opt)`?
That's why I added it and I guess I was thinking the pipeline would have caught cases where programs were depending on ws_log_parse_args.
What "tests" can I run locally to flush out all of the cases where ws_log_is_wslog_arg is needed?
I think there are tests for most all of the command line tools, adding some log related option like `--log-fatal-domains=UTF-8` or `--log-level=message` to one for each program should work.
"Manually" or do you think I should modify the pytest (or similar) code to have this caught in the future?

I think it would be good to add it to the tests. I think one reason why they aren't in the tests is because of the very issue with memory corruption on Windows that this fixed - I remember there being an issue with some tests failing on Windows when they tried to write to the logs .
resolved all threads

> This "works" but wanted feedback on if it's the right approach in terms of encapsulation/layering.

No it's not the right approach. The wslog API was very carefully and deliberately designed and this MR introduces a remarkable amount of pessifications just to fix a trivial memory issue artificially introduced in cli_main by some macro magic. You received good feedback in #20500 and you should have followed it.

Modifying data structures in general and argv/argc specifically (which you'll note is explicitly permitted by ISO C) in no way prevents cli_main from using memory, allocating memory, freeing memory or really implementing any number of trivial and sensible fixes for the memory bug you found.

There is also a reason the argument parsing solution is "independent", everything depends on wslog so its transitive dependencies must be absolutely minimal. Adding a dependency on ws_getopt.h for every single file that uses logging (and that is all of them) is not OK.

In the interest of time and space we can stop here but describing wslog as "a little more self-contained before" is somewhat akin to describing malignant cancer as "a tiny eeny bit of excess cell growth".

>>>
wslog needs to share the "application" options because ws_getopt needs to know the "properties" of an option (and if they have a required argument) in order to properly parse any/all of them (as I found out testing with pytest)
>>>

No, argument sharing (two-way no less!) is only required because you introduced an unnecessary and detrimental (and frankly ugly) getopt() dependency to wslog and this MR didn't fix anything in wslog specifically, very much the contrary.

The "command line argument parsing functionality" (getopt for short) should be able to provide a list of all supported options for an application.  In that sense, wslog was "hiding" its options from the applications and that's why I leaned into "being more explicit" with the long options supported by each application.  And that led me to the "code reuse" of getopt, which also happened to fix the memory issue.  The sole reason for the MR wasn't to find a fix for the memory issue.

wslog and ws_getopt are both part of the same library, wsutil and they have enough "Wireshark specifics" in them that I don't see them ever being separated making the dependency an issue.

You also made the `console.log.level` preference broken *again*. One presumes logging should be usable before preferences are parsed and that the logging preference setting is required for that. Otherwise you should just remove it instead of confusing everyone. It's already confusing enough as it is and only kept for backward compatibility purposes.
I'll submit a new MR to fix that.

> The "command line argument parsing functionality" (getopt for short) should be able to provide a list of all supported options for an application. In that sense, wslog was "hiding" its options from the applications and that's why I leaned into "being more explicit" with the long options supported by each application.

I do not understand what this means, sorry. I don't know of any lists not being provided. Does this MR provide any new user facing functionality? The answer is "no" as far as I can tell. Does it improve anything otherwise? Definitely not. "getopt" is just one particular and somewhat limited library that implements argument parsing whose main strengths are being simple and standardized by POSIX.

Again hiding many implementation details and reducing shared state was precisely one of the main goals. Encapsulation, DRY, separation of concerns, etc., all basic principles of strong software engineering that were weakened by this MR and that I don't feel like drilling into because this isn't a homework school assignement.

This MR has no redeeming qualities whatsoever and is just a workaround for what is clearly a bug in cli_main. A bug which is still latent by the way, despite your extensive unimprovement of wslog and general increase of the maintenance burden. You can't just use macro magic to silently change the standard norms and practices of how main() operates in C and then blame something else for relying on those same norms and practices. The conditions that created the bug are understandable, your flawed analysis and reaction is not in my opinion.

I can assure you that the devs who carefully designed and successfully deployed wslog have already considered this rather obvious and ugly way of doing split argument parsing and discarded it as inferior because getopt() is not the right tool for this job (among other reasons).

> The sole reason for the MR wasn't to find a fix for the memory issue.

That is even worse. It is one thing to try to build up something new and come up short. That can happen and is generally not a big deal. Tearing down something that is already painstakingly built up to a high standard for no good reason is on another level entirely and much more upsetting.

Good luck.

If you're so fixated and dead-set on using getopt for argument parsing, I suppose you could replace the wslog hand rolled argument parsing while loop with getopt and ignore unknown arguments. I haven't looked into it in detail and I don't remember every getopt quirk off the top of my head but it should be doable and that is just a small implementation detail. getopt is just a function implementing one big loop itself after all. It changes almost nothing.

The important detail here is to make the new getopt dependency private to wslog in that case and not force every other program and utility to handle wslog arguments using macro hacks and shared state and vice-versa. That should make anyone sad.

You already had to fix one name clash in pcapio.c to prove my point, if more proof were needed.

The convention is that wslog arguments must start with `--log-`. That was intentional so they can be easily ignored but it is not used in practice because it wasn't required due to the superior design of *removing already parsed arguments from argv*.

I think the point of contention is how to slice the layering/encapsulation of parsing command line parameters regardless of feature.  wslog is just the first/only that tells the application "let me secretly handle my own parameters.  I won't tell you what they are (so they may clash with other options in the future), but trust me you want them".  I would argue wslog's interface to applications shouldn't be passing in argv/argc data in the first place, that just seemed like the "simplest" at the time if only looking at that feature and not a bigger picture of how _all_ parameters are parsed (this "encapsulation" caused a "repeat yourself" of having to roll its own argument parsing).  All other features have a "set" call by the application (acknowledging an "opt in" of the feature), so why should wslog be different?  Given getopt's current implementation, could that mean wslog's integration would be a macro of a many case statements of its options with "set" calls within the application's current while loop switch statement?  Yes, but I didn't decide to take it that far (but the thought exercise crossed my mind).  It's not that I like getopt that much, I just consider it the standard that all applications in the repo should adhere to, so if we change the "command line parsing interface" to something other than getopt (highly unlikely, I know), we know what the interface is.

I don't have a strong opinion on what should be done with invalid/unknown command line parameters (silently ignore or cause application to fail), but I'd probably lean "silently ignore" (or at least not a complete fail of application).  The "cause application to fail" that most applications in the repo have has definitely made the wslog feature look "less encapsulated" when it's not stealing argc/argv data, but was done to keep backwards compatibility.

I've also considered adding support for getopt to "remove" parameters like wslog was previously doing.  And then we would reintroduce the cli_main bug (and potentially fix it in the way Guy suggested)

As far as I'm concerned the point of contention is that your change didn't fix or improve anything and has several significant downsides. Usually there is some tradeoff to be considered but here I don't see any, it's all negatives.

There is no clash of arguments or secrecy dilemma involved either.

At this point I do not know how to make that case better or more forcefully.

I'm not sure I understand the problem you are trying to solve (other than working around a cli_main bug) but to try to address the concern you raised a different module or main program wanting to add an option to the `--log-*` namespace would be a really bad idea and should be strongly discouraged.

There are very many good reasons why wslog is special. One is that logging should be ready very early in the startup process and it cannot depend on anything else that uses logging. That would introduce a circular dependency that is problematic.

For example if you wanted to use logging in `ws_getopt`, which is a reasonable thing to want to do, it would be a bad idea to have wslog depend on `ws_getopt` for configuration.

I still don't see how your MR minimizes any potential clashes or where secrecy comes into play.

You added a convoluted and inefficient way for main to ignore unknown arguments, namely `ws_log_is_wslog_arg`. I will argue all day that removing these arguments, call it hiding or whatever, is the better solution.
@mmann78 Since clearly I'm the only one who doesn't like this MR or cares enough to review it, then by all means keep it as is. Don't even worry about it. I hope my feedback was helpful.

commits_data.title: Fix wslog parameters altering command line arguments
commits_data.message:
Fix wslog parameters altering command line arguments

Convert wslog subsystem to use ws_getopt subsystem to parse the command line arguments it's interested in rather than a independent solution that can modify the argc/argv parameters provided to an application. This way the argc/argv parameters aren't ever modified and cli_main.c can "own" their memory (and allocate and free as needed).
This means that all applications that use ws_log subsystem must provide the ws_log command line arguments in their list of "long" (command line) options so ws_get_options can know the "properties" of all options (and things like if the option requires an argument)

Also rename ws_option -> ws_option_tlv used in pcapio.c because it conflicts with the "more popular" structure used to parse options.

Fix #20500
